newsitem.title: NORWAY: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND THROWS DOWN CHALLENGE TO AAMODT.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND THROWS DOWN CHALLENGE TO AAMODT.

text.p: Luc Alphand accomplished what he set out to do on Sunday, winning one World Cup title and tightening his grip on two others.
With bad weather forcing officials to run a rescheduled downhill in the morning and a super-G in the afternoon, it was a busy and productive 12 hours for the 31-year-old Frenchman.
Alphand began the day by clinching his third consecutive downhill World Cup title after finishing fifth behind Norwegian winner Lasse Kjus.
A few hours later Alphand finished joint fourth with Austria's Hermann Maier in the super-G to keep a 69-point lead in the rankings with only one race remaining.
But most importantly, the two results combined to leave him 193 points clear of Norway's Kjetil Andre Aamodt in the battle for the overall crown.
"I skied much the same in the super-G as I did in the downhill, aggressive but safe," said Alphand, who aims to become the first Frenchman to win the overall title since Jean-Claude Killy in 1968.
"I'm content because I still have a strong chance to clinch the super-G title.
"My goal in the overall was to stay around 200 points ahead of Aamodt so now let's see what he can do in Japan."
By outscoring Aamodt on his home snow Alphand has placed the ball squarely in the Norwegian's court.
Aamodt will have to win both the giant slalom and slalom races in Japan next weekend if he wants to erase the Frenchman's advantage before they arrive in Vail for the World Cup finals.
"I wasn't able to take advantage of my chances here to score points," said Aamodt, who was seventh in the downhill and ninth in the super-G. "It will be difficult now to catch Alphand."
Aamodt was hoping to have the same type of weekend his team mate Kjus enjoyed, winning the downhill and placing third in the super-G.

It did not start out as a great weekend for Kjus either. He was denied victory on Saturday when high winds forced officials to rule the downhill invalid just two skiers short of declaring it official.
But the 26-year-old Norwegian refused to be denied a second time as he returned to the top of the podium on Sunday.
Led by Josef Strobl, Austrians dominated the super-G and claimed three of the top four places.
After a steady downpour had twice delayed the start, the skies suddenly cleared allowing officials to proceed.
Ignoring the soggy conditions Strobl sloshed his way down the 2,418-metre Olympiabakken course to claim his first super-G win and third World Cup victory of his career.
Austria's Andreas Schifferer was second followed by Kjus who crossed just ahead of Maier and Alphand.
